name: Circuit product capability model
purpose: A current-checkout baseline that separates user outcomes from controls, guarantees, mechanisms, and the surfaces that expose or prove them.

baseline.note: Current-checkout census rebuilt for v0.2 with typed evidence, derived reach, and explicit surface dispositions.

vision.title: Encode the process
vision.statement: Turn a known way of working into a repeatable, invokable, adjustable flow.

vision.title: Fit the worker to the step
vision.statement: Give each step the right role, context, tools, connector, model, and effort.

vision.title: Require proof before progress
vision.statement: Do not advance or close until the declared evidence exists and parses.

vision.title: Carry the operational load
vision.statement: Carry routing, state, coordination, recovery, and continuity outside the chat.

vision.title: Improve from experience
vision.statement: Use evidence from real runs to improve the process that runs next time.

areas.title: Shape intent into a repeatable process
areas.summary: Move from an operator's intent to an authored process with a clear boundary and proof plan.

areas.title: Apply skilled work patterns
areas.summary: Offer proven processes for recurring kinds of product and engineering work.

areas.title: Equip and coordinate agents
areas.summary: Give each step the right working conditions and coordinate bounded forms of parallel and repeated work.

areas.title: Preserve confidence and continuity
areas.summary: Make work understandable before it starts and recoverable after pauses, failures, or session changes.

areas.title: Prove and explain outcomes
areas.summary: Check the work, judge it separately, and leave an honest record of what happened.

areas.title: Learn and improve from experience
areas.summary: Capture useful lessons, bring them back at the right time, and improve flows from real evidence.

areas.title: Configure and operate Circuit
areas.summary: Keep Circuit understandable, ready, configurable, and removable across supported environments.

capabilities.title: Route a request into the right flow
capabilities.outcome: Turn an operator request into the most suitable authored process.

claims.statement: Turn an operator request into the most suitable authored process.

refs.proves: Defines the behavior: Turn an operator request into the most suitable authored process.

attention.note: Hosts can recommend a flow, but the CLI still expects the caller to choose one explicitly.

capabilities.title: Frame the outcome, limits, and proof
capabilities.outcome: Turn a rough request into a bounded brief with a declared way to prove success.

claims.statement: A released Build run records a bounded brief and stops at the frame checkpoint before implementation.

refs.proves: Registers a verified explicit Build run whose evidence includes the Build brief and frame checkpoint.
Shows the checked-in brief produced by that verified run.

capabilities.title: Create, customize, publish, and manage flows
capabilities.outcome: Carry a custom process through a complete lifecycle, not just its first generation.

claims.statement: Draft and publish a runnable custom flow only after explicit confirmation, preserving the reviewed draft.

refs.proves: Exercises runnable draft creation, explicit publish confirmation, and publication of the reviewed draft bytes.
Exercises the create command's validate-and-publish path and its confirmation boundary.

attention.note: Create and generate exist, but version, share, supersede, retire, and host publication are not one complete lifecycle.

capabilities.title: Audit existing work
capabilities.outcome: Inspect a bounded body of work and report evidence-backed findings without changing it.

claims.statement: Inspect a bounded body of work and report evidence-backed findings without changing it.

refs.proves: Attests the released outcome: Inspect a bounded body of work and report evidence-backed findings without changing it.

capabilities.title: Fix broken behavior
capabilities.outcome: Diagnose a fault, change the smallest useful surface, and verify the repair.

claims.statement: Diagnose a fault, change the smallest useful surface, and verify the repair.

refs.proves: Attests the released outcome: Diagnose a fault, change the smallest useful surface, and verify the repair.

capabilities.title: Build a change
capabilities.outcome: Frame, implement, verify, and review a deliberate product or engineering change.

claims.statement: Frame, implement, verify, and review a deliberate product or engineering change.

refs.proves: Attests the released outcome: Frame, implement, verify, and review a deliberate product or engineering change.

capabilities.title: Explore a question or decision
capabilities.outcome: Gather evidence, compare real options, and make a bounded recommendation.

claims.statement: Gather evidence, compare real options, and make a bounded recommendation.

refs.proves: Attests the released outcome: Gather evidence, compare real options, and make a bounded recommendation.

capabilities.title: Prototype and compare disposable solutions
capabilities.outcome: Build a cheap learning artifact and use it to choose what deserves a real implementation.

claims.statement: Build a cheap learning artifact and use it to choose what deserves a real implementation.

refs.proves: Attests the released outcome: Build a cheap learning artifact and use it to choose what deserves a real implementation.

capabilities.title: Own a bounded outcome across several pieces of work
capabilities.outcome: Keep pursuing a declared outcome through bounded attempts, evaluation, and recovery.

claims.statement: Keep pursuing a declared outcome through bounded attempts, evaluation, and recovery.

refs.proves: Exercises Goal completion only after a satisfied evaluation and two completion gates, while unresolved child results cannot count as proof.

attention.note: Outcome ownership and queue-and-batch both address work larger than one simple flow.

capabilities.title: Craft explanatory artifacts for humans
capabilities.outcome: Turn source material into a polished artifact made for human readers rather than code review.

claims.statement: Turn source material into a polished artifact made for human readers rather than code review.

refs.proves: Defines the behavior: Turn source material into a polished artifact made for human readers rather than code review.

attention.note: The active Explainer flow is a source-checkout flow, not a generated public host flow.

capabilities.title: Preview execution before spending
capabilities.outcome: Show the planned worker, connector, model, and effort choices without starting a run.

claims.statement: Show the planned worker, connector, model, and effort choices without starting a run.

refs.proves: Exercises spend-free previews of step count, connector resolution, model tier, and effort across power settings.

capabilities.title: Resolve a checkpoint and continue safely
capabilities.outcome: Answer a bounded checkpoint decision and continue from its saved state without losing the evidence boundary.

claims.statement: A saved checkpoint can accept an operator choice, restore its bound state, and continue the graph.

refs.proves: Exercises resuming a paused Build checkpoint through an operator selection.
Exercises restoring saved checkpoint context, continuing the graph, and rejecting a changed evidence boundary.

capabilities.title: Run unattended within authored bounds
capabilities.outcome: Auto-resolve supported checkpoints in a bounded continuation loop that can never close complete by exhaustion.

claims.statement: Auto-resolve supported checkpoints in a bounded continuation loop that can never close complete by exhaustion.

refs.proves: Exercises the live autonomous continuation loop, persists its result, and leaves the default non-autonomous path unchanged.

capabilities.title: Resume work parked at a checkpoint
capabilities.outcome: Continue a durable run from a declared checkpoint; Codex can rediscover and resume it after the MCP host restarts.

claims.statement: Checkpoint resume works in the CLI, and Codex can resume after an MCP restart.

refs.proves: Exercises CLI resume from a declared checkpoint.
Exercises Codex rediscovery and resume after an MCP process restart.

capabilities.title: Carry work across sessions
capabilities.outcome: Persist the state, evidence, and next action another session needs to continue safely.

claims.statement: An operator can save standalone continuity, resume it in a later invocation, and clear it when finished.

refs.proves: Exercises saving, resuming, and clearing a standalone handoff record through the CLI.

capabilities.title: Recover and clean up safely
capabilities.outcome: Reclaim resources safely; Codex recovery closes an exact recoverable run without claiming to continue it.

claims.statement: Codex recovery is state-checked, closes the old run, and never resumes it.

refs.proves: Exercises recovery-required state checks and recovery after lifecycle restart.
States that recovery closes the old run and does not continue it.

capabilities.title: Control a durable Codex run
capabilities.outcome: Start, watch, resume, cancel, list, and recover a durable run through Codex without replacing its lifecycle with shell commands.

claims.statement: Codex exposes start, status, resume, cancel, list, and recover as six typed lifecycle tools.

refs.proves: Registers the exact six lifecycle tool names and typed contracts.
Exercises the durable start, polling, resume, cancel, list, and recovery lifecycle.

attention.note: Durable lifecycle control is shipped through Codex MCP, while CLI and Claude remain attached or command-driven.

capabilities.title: Close honestly with evidence, risks, and follow-ups
capabilities.outcome: End with an outcome the available evidence supports, explained in operator-readable close-out artifacts, and preserve what remains unresolved.

claims.statement: End with an outcome the available evidence supports, explained in operator-readable close-out artifacts, and preserve what remains unresolved.

refs.proves: Exercises evidence-backed operator summaries with honest outcomes, risks, and follow-ups.

capabilities.title: Inspect recorded and active runs
capabilities.outcome: Find recorded and active work, inspect trace and evidence, and use Codex list and status to rediscover durable runs.

claims.statement: CLI history and runs plus Codex list and status expose durable run inspection.

refs.proves: Exercises CLI history listing and inspection.
Exercises Codex list and status after a lifecycle restart.

attention.note: Codex list and status are both inspection tools and part of its durable control lifecycle.

capabilities.title: Follow a run while it happens
capabilities.outcome: Watch structured progress while attached through the CLI or reconnect by polling durable Codex status from the last cursor.

claims.statement: CLI streams progress and Codex status supports cursor-based polling and bounded waits.

refs.proves: Exercises schema-shaped CLI progress events.
Exercises cursor-based Codex status polling and bounded waits.

attention.note: Codex status provides both reconnectable progress following and lifecycle control state.

capabilities.title: Capture operator lessons with evidence provenance
capabilities.outcome: Record a durable lesson and preserve where it came from so it can be judged later.

claims.statement: Record a durable lesson and preserve where it came from so it can be judged later.

refs.proves: Exercises writing a project lesson tied to the current run, listing it, and removing it.

capabilities.title: Reuse relevant evidence from earlier runs
capabilities.outcome: Bring prior facts and lessons into later work without making the operator reconstruct them from chat.

claims.statement: Bring prior facts and lessons into later work without making the operator reconstruct them from chat.

refs.proves: Exercises rebuilding local history, writing a recall report, and adding hint-only memory to later relay prompts.

capabilities.title: Measure whether a lesson helped
capabilities.outcome: Judge each remembered lesson against later run outcomes and stop surfacing the ones that measurably hurt.

claims.statement: Judge each remembered lesson against later run outcomes and stop surfacing the ones that measurably hurt.

refs.proves: Exercises positive, negative, unresolved, and insufficient-data effect verdicts with adverse-outcome safeguards.
Exercises flow-scoped recall, a bounded push set, and an always-present precision record.
Exercises suppressing only flow-matched lessons measured as harmful while preserving other recalled material.

capabilities.title: Measure, promote, and improve flows
capabilities.outcome: Use evidence from completed work to create or revise a reusable process with a measurable reason.

claims.statement: Use evidence from completed work to create or revise a reusable process with a measurable reason.

refs.proves: Describes the proposed outcome: Use evidence from completed work to create or revise a reusable process with a measurable reason.

attention.note: Run evidence does not yet revise or promote a flow automatically or through one measured workflow.

capabilities.title: Configure routing, connectors, models, power, and skills
capabilities.outcome: Set worker and connector selection, models, power, process rigor, and local skills without confusing that policy with flow routing.

claims.statement: Typed configuration applies defaults, rejects unknown policy keys, and registers trusted custom connectors with write limits.

refs.proves: Exercises configuration defaults, supported overrides, schema versioning, and rejection of misspelled keys.
Exercises trusted custom connector resolution and rejection of read-only connectors for write work.

capabilities.title: Check readiness, version, and runtime provenance
capabilities.outcome: Explain whether Circuit can run here, which build is active, and what needs to be fixed.

claims.statement: Explain whether Circuit can run here, which build is active, and what needs to be fixed.

refs.proves: Exercises ready and broken connector verdicts, resolution-source labels, and copyable fixes.

capabilities.title: Maintain or remove the installation and leftover resources
capabilities.outcome: Keep installed host bridges and local run resources understandable and removable.

claims.statement: Circuit can remove its marked host integration blocks without damaging surrounding configuration.

refs.proves: Exercises removing one or more marked install blocks, preserving surrounding text, and refusing malformed markers.

attention.note: Uninstall, host-hook maintenance, and orphan-worktree cleanup are separate utilities rather than one installation lifecycle.

capabilities.title: Operate the same flows from multiple agent hosts
capabilities.outcome: Use the same encoded flows from Claude Code, Codex, or a shell through host-specific bridges whose lifecycle shapes are not identical.

claims.statement: Claude and Codex reach the same encoded flow packages through different host bridges.

refs.proves: Exercises the installed Claude command bridge and generated public flow package.
Exercises the Codex plugin package, skills, flow catalog, and MCP bridge.

attention.note: Claude drives the CLI bridge while Codex owns a six-tool MCP lifecycle; feature reach is not identical.

capabilities.title: Orient and discover without reading docs
capabilities.outcome: Give a bare invocation, a piped agent, or a lost operator a guided path to the right next command.

claims.statement: Give a bare invocation, a piped agent, or a lost operator a guided path to the right next command.

refs.proves: Exercises the orientation page and command help with usage, examples, aliases, and copyable next commands.

capabilities.title: Install Circuit
capabilities.outcome: Install Circuit through the Claude Code plugin, the Codex plugin and MCP bridge, or the local CLI path.

claims.statement: Circuit packages installable Claude and Codex host bridges and verifies their bundled runtime contracts.

refs.proves: Exercises the installed Claude plugin wrapper and its packaged engine.
Exercises the installable Codex plugin tree and MCP package contract.
Exercises host-package publication metadata, user installation effects, and installed-byte validation.

claims.statement: The release gate installs the packed npm artifact in an isolated prefix and invokes its public CLI.

refs.proves: Defines the packed npm install and public CLI invocation required by check-release-infra.

capabilities.title: Try Circuit in a safe demo
capabilities.outcome: Run one real Fix flow against a throwaway project without changing the current checkout.

claims.statement: The demo creates a throwaway project with a real bug and runs the real Fix path there.

refs.proves: Creates and targets an isolated temporary project.
Exercises isolation, the real Fix invocation, and demo cleanup.

capabilities.title: Use a custom connector
capabilities.outcome: Register a trusted prompt-file and output-file worker connector and select it for compatible read-only steps.

claims.statement: Trusted configuration can register a custom connector while runtime safety rejects incompatible write work.

refs.proves: Defines registered custom connector descriptors and selection references.
Exercises trusted custom resolution and rejection of read-only connectors for implementer work.

supporting_elements.title: Encode typed flows from blocks, routes, and checks
supporting_elements.summary: Describe a reusable process as authored topology with typed seams and evidence requirements.

claims.statement: Describe a reusable process as authored topology with typed seams and evidence requirements.

refs.proves: Exercises catalog-to-schematic parity, exact production flow IDs, and connector selection through composed branches.

supporting_elements.title: Run isolated, role-shaped steps with scoped context and tools
supporting_elements.summary: Give a worker only the role, context, skills, and tools needed for one bounded step.

claims.statement: Give a worker only the role, context, skills, and tools needed for one bounded step.

refs.proves: Exercises trusted and enforced tool scopes, including safe downgrade when a connector cannot restrict tools.

supporting_elements.title: Allocate connector, model, and effort per step
supporting_elements.summary: Choose the worker and spend level from the step's role, with explicit overrides when needed.

claims.statement: Choose the worker and spend level from the step's role, with explicit overrides when needed.

refs.proves: Exercises role-based connector, model-tier, and effort selection across low, medium, high, and auto power.

supporting_elements.title: Sequence, route, nest, and continue work within authored bounds
supporting_elements.summary: Execute an authored graph whose next steps are constrained by declared routes and child-flow seams.

claims.statement: Execute an authored graph whose next steps are constrained by declared routes and child-flow seams.

refs.proves: Exercises that the assembled Goal schematic and compiled child-flow graph match the package loaded by the runtime.

supporting_elements.title: Fan out and compare alternatives
supporting_elements.summary: Run bounded alternatives independently, gather comparable evidence, and join them for a decision.

claims.statement: Run bounded alternatives independently, gather comparable evidence, and join them for a decision.

refs.proves: Exercises real child-flow execution for every fan-out branch and admission through the aggregate result.

supporting_elements.title: Iterate until declared evidence passes
supporting_elements.summary: Repeat a bounded body while its authored condition says the proof is not yet sufficient.

claims.statement: Repeat a bounded body while its authored condition says the proof is not yet sufficient.

refs.proves: Exercises repeated full-body execution, single-pass fallback, route validation, and authored iteration bounds.

supporting_elements.title: Queue and batch broad work
supporting_elements.summary: Turn broad work into ordered items and process a bounded set with explicit outcomes.

claims.statement: Turn broad work into ordered items and process a bounded set with explicit outcomes.

refs.proves: Exercises the internal Pursue path through coordination, bounded batch work, verification, review, and close.

attention.note: Queue-and-batch machinery overlaps the broader outcome-ownership shape and remains internal.

supporting_elements.title: Route runtime signals to the operator's skills
supporting_elements.summary: Fire a declared hook when a runtime signal matches and inject the operator's skill into the next relevant worker step.

claims.statement: Fire a declared hook when a runtime signal matches and inject the operator's skill into the next relevant worker step.

refs.proves: Exercises matching an active hook, recording its policy decision, and injecting only resolved skills into the next relay.

attention.note: Four hook anchors are live; seven accepted names remain reserved and inert.

disposition.reason: Keep reserved names visible as dormant vocabulary until runtime dispatch exists.

supporting_elements.title: Scale rigor and spend to the stakes
supporting_elements.summary: Set how much process and model power a run deserves, or let the run recommend a level within declared limits.

claims.statement: Set how much process and model power a run deserves, or let the run recommend a level within declared limits.

refs.proves: Exercises power defaults and precedence plus role-specific model or effort tiers for Claude and Codex.

supporting_elements.title: Adapt a running flow within bounds
supporting_elements.summary: Let a confirmed runtime discovery adjust later steps' skills, or let a step pull one typed context slice, without changing the authored topology.

claims.statement: A confirmed runtime discovery can re-resolve equipment for later relay steps without changing the authored graph.

refs.proves: Exercises injecting newly resolved equipment after a confirmed discovery and withholding it when the discovery is unconfirmed.

attention.note: Equipment reshaping and typed context pulls work internally but have no direct operator surface.

disposition.reason: Keep adaptation as an internal control while its user promise is still unsettled.

supporting_elements.title: Capture session state automatically
supporting_elements.summary: Harvest a continuity record from the live session with no operator action, as a safety net under deliberate handoffs.

claims.statement: Harvest a continuity record from the live session with no operator action, as a safety net under deliberate handoffs.

refs.proves: Exercises harvesting genuine session intent and compaction context while preserving a deliberate handoff as the primary record.

attention.note: Ambient harvest is a safety net beneath deliberate cross-session handoff, not a competing source of truth.

disposition.reason: Keep both: deliberate handoff leads, ambient continuity catches missed saves.

supporting_elements.title: Run deterministic checks
supporting_elements.summary: Execute declared proof commands and capture their result as run evidence.

claims.statement: Execute declared proof commands and capture their result as run evidence.

refs.proves: Exercises passed, failed, missing, unsafe, timed-out, and unlaunchable verification commands with typed evidence.

supporting_elements.title: Judge results independently
supporting_elements.summary: Separate doing the work from deciding whether the result satisfies its brief.

claims.statement: Separate doing the work from deciding whether the result satisfies its brief.

refs.proves: Exercises a separate reviewer relay whose clean or blocking findings determine the recorded close outcome.

supporting_elements.title: Block false claims of done
supporting_elements.summary: Check worker claims against ground truth and refuse a clean close while any overclaim or tampered proof stands.

claims.statement: Check worker claims against ground truth and refuse a clean close while any overclaim or tampered proof stands.

refs.proves: Exercises durable overclaim latches and the finalize-time gap that blocks a clean close while a latch remains open.
Exercises rejecting a worker's claimed changed file when the working tree does not support that claim.
Exercises detecting modified, created, and deleted files on a declared frozen evaluation surface.
Exercises a tampered evaluation surface opening an integrity latch and preventing an otherwise accepted run from closing complete.

supporting_elements.title: Require consent for sensitive host data and write access
supporting_elements.summary: Keep cached web search off by default, gate untracked review contents, and disclose write-capable workers before edits.

claims.statement: Codex input and connector policies keep data and write boundaries explicit.

refs.proves: Exercises the off-by-default web search contract and bounded opt-in values.
Exercises explicit consent before including untracked Review content and a write-capability warning before Build waits for framing approval.
Exercises read-only, isolated-write, and trusted-write connector policy.

boundaries.title: No fully dynamic runtime-composed workflows
boundaries.rule: Circuit prefers authored topology with typed seams over an open-ended runtime classifier.

refs.proves: Records the product boundary: Circuit prefers authored topology with typed seams over an open-ended runtime classifier.
Records the product boundary: Circuit prefers authored topology with typed seams over an open-ended runtime classifier.

boundaries.title: No git-push interception
boundaries.rule: Circuit routes work through deliberately invoked flows rather than a hook that captures every push.

refs.proves: Records the product boundary: Circuit routes work through deliberately invoked flows rather than a hook that captures every push.

boundaries.title: No keep-best optimization loop without an ungameable judge
boundaries.rule: Exhaust-and-keep-best would weaken the evidence and honesty model without a trustworthy oracle.

refs.proves: Records the product boundary: Exhaust-and-keep-best would weaken the evidence and honesty model without a trustworthy oracle.
Records the product boundary: Exhaust-and-keep-best would weaken the evidence and honesty model without a trustworthy oracle.

boundaries.title: No mid-task model switching by runtime guess
boundaries.rule: Worker allocation is authored per step rather than delegated to an opaque runtime classifier.

refs.proves: Records the product boundary: Worker allocation is authored per step rather than delegated to an opaque runtime classifier.

boundaries.title: Memory guides, never governs
boundaries.rule: Recalled lessons are cited hints; they never change routes, checkpoints, or proofs, and Circuit claims no self-improvement until measured effect earns it.

refs.proves: Records the product boundary: Recalled lessons are cited hints; they never change routes, checkpoints, or proofs, and Circuit claims no self-improvement until measured effect earns it.
Records the product boundary: Recalled lessons are cited hints; they never change routes, checkpoints, or proofs, and Circuit claims no self-improvement until measured effect earns it.

boundaries.title: No universal percentage and no invented ETA
boundaries.rule: Progress reports known structure only; an estimate appears only when flow-specific evidence supports it.

refs.proves: Records the product boundary: Progress reports known structure only; an estimate appears only when flow-specific evidence supports it.

boundaries.title: No generic pause button and no free-form mid-worker steering
boundaries.rule: Mid-run influence arrives only through declared checkpoints and bounded channels, not an open steering wheel.

refs.proves: Records the product boundary: Mid-run influence arrives only through declared checkpoints and bounded channels, not an open steering wheel.

boundaries.title: Hosts never become the orchestrator
boundaries.rule: Host-native execution stays an adapter under Circuit's authority so every client shares one capability model.

refs.proves: Records the product boundary: Host-native execution stays an adapter under Circuit's authority so every client shares one capability model.
Records the product boundary: Host-native execution stays an adapter under Circuit's authority so every client shares one capability model.

boundaries.title: Internal flows are examples or proof
boundaries.rule: An internal flow can prove a mechanism without creating a public product promise.

refs.proves: Records public and internal flow visibility separately.

boundaries.title: Codex recovery closes the old run
boundaries.rule: circuit_recover applies only to recovery-required work and never continues the old run.

refs.proves: States the exact Codex recovery boundary.

boundaries.title: Custom connector commands come only from trusted configuration
boundaries.rule: Repository-controlled configuration cannot inject arbitrary connector commands, and read-only connectors cannot implement changes.

refs.proves: Exercises trusted command provenance and write compatibility checks.

review_questions.question: Should Run become the one product front door that chooses a flow, or should explicit flow choice remain part of the contract?
What is the smallest complete custom-flow lifecycle worth making public?
With Goal frozen into the run envelope, what public shape, if any, should Pursue and its queue-and-batch machinery take?
Which internal coordination mechanics deserve a public product surface, and which should remain implementation proof?
Which durable run controls should reach CLI and Claude, and which should remain Codex-specific?
What evidence must exist before the learning loop is allowed to change a flow?
Which CLI-only utilities are real product surfaces, and which are maintenance details that should stay out of the primary map?
Should Circuit compute dependable per-run time and cost estimates, or does cost candor stay static documentation?
Which capabilities must reach both hosts at parity, and where is asymmetry acceptable?
